source_text: [1] Ἀπὸ Συρίας μέχρι Ῥώμης θηριομαχῶ, διὰ γῆς καὶ θαλάσσης, νυκτὸς καὶ ἧμερας, δεδεμένος δέκα λεοπάρδοις, ὅ ἐστιν στρατιωτικὸν τάγμα: οἲ καὶ εὐεργετούμενοι χείρους γίνονται. ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἀδικήμασιν αὐτῶν μᾶλλον μαθητεύομαι, ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο δεδικαίωμαι. [2] ὀναίμην τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἐμοὶ ἡτοιμασμένων καὶ εὔχομαι σύντομά μοι εὑρεθῆναι: ἃ καὶ κολακεύσω, συντόμως με καταφαγεῖν, οὐχ ὥσπερ τινῶν δειλαινόμενα οὐχ ἥψαντο. κἂν αὐτὰ δὲ ἄκοντα μὴ θελήσῃ, ἐγὼ προσβιάσομαι. [3] συγγνώμην μοι ἔχετε: τί μοι συμφέρει, ἐγὼ γινώσκω, νῦν ἄρχομαι μαθητὴς εἶναι. μηθέν με ζηλώσαι τῶν ὁρατῶν καὶ ἀοράτων, ἵνα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιτύχω. πῦρ καὶ σταυρὸς θηρίων τε συστάσεις, ἀνατομαί, διαιρέσεις, σκορπισμοὶ ὀστέων, συγκοπὴ μελῶν, ἀλεσμοὶ ὅλου τοῦ σώματος, κακαὶ κολάσεις τοῦ διαβόλου ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ἐρχέσθωσαν, μόνον ἵνα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιτύχω.
pass_a_gloss: From Syria as far as Rome I fight with beasts, through land and sea, by night and by day, bound to ten leopards, which is a detachment of soldiers, who even when they are treated well become worse. But by their wrongdoings I am more made a disciple, but I am not justified by this. May I have joy of the beasts that have been prepared for me, and I pray they may be found prompt for me; I will even coax them to devour me promptly, not as with some whom, being cowardly, they did not touch. And even if they themselves, unwilling, do not want to, I will force them. Have forgiveness for me: what is profitable for me, I know. Now I am beginning to be a disciple. May nothing of things visible and invisible envy me, so that I may attain to Jesus Christ. Fire and cross and packs of beasts, cuttings, tearings apart, scatterings of bones, mangling of limbs, grindings of the whole body, evil torments of the devil, let them come upon me, only that I may attain to Jesus Christ.
pass_b_english: From Syria to Rome I am fighting beasts, by land and sea, by night and day, chained to ten leopards, a squad of soldiers, who only get worse when they are treated well. Their abuse makes me more of a disciple, yet that is not what makes me righteous (1 Corinthians 4:4).

May I have the joy of the beasts made ready for me, and I pray they will be quick with me. I will even coax them to devour me quickly, not as they did with some, whom they were too timid to touch. And if they hold back and will not, I will force them.

Forgive me; I know what is good for me. Now I am beginning to be a disciple. Let nothing seen or unseen grudge me this, that I may reach Jesus Christ. Fire and cross and packs of beasts, cutting and tearing, the scattering of bones, the mangling of limbs, the grinding of my whole body, the devil's cruel tortures: let them come upon me, if only I may reach Jesus Christ.

choices.why: the image that names the game; Ignatius glosses it himself as soldiers

choices.english: that is not what makes me righteous (1 Corinthians 4:4)
choices.why: verbatim echo of Paul's οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωμαι
ζηλόω here is envious grudging of his prize

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Greek 'Ἀπὸ Συρίας μέχρι Ῥώμης θηριομαχῶ, διὰ γῆς καὶ θαλάσσης' matches A 'From Syria as far as Rome I fight with beasts, through land and sea' and B 'From Syria to Rome I am fighting beasts, by land and sea'. 'ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο δεδικαίωμαι' keeps the denial in A 'but I am not justified by this' and B 'yet that is not what makes me righteous (1 Corinthians 4:4)'; the added citation agrees with the supplied wording note and is not a wrong verse. 'κἂν αὐτὰ δὲ ἄκοντα μὴ θελήσῃ, ἐγὼ προσβιάσομαι' is fully in A 'And even if they themselves, unwilling, do not want to, I will force them'; B 'And if they hold back and will not, I will force them' compresses without reversing who forces or that the beasts are unwilling. Title 'Chained to ten leopards' names the thought.

All source clauses accounted for in Pass A and B: Greek paragraph [1] fully rendered; negation (οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο δεδικαίωμαι) preserved with correct 1 Corinthians 4:4 citation; agency (I will force them) clear; modality (may I have joy, I pray) preserved; doctrinal distinction (disciple vs justified) maintained; scripture citation correctly identified and added per apparatus note. Title 'Chained to ten leopards' captures the Ignatian gloss as names the thought. OCR damage noted in variants/kἂn clause handled per witness note. No omissions, additions, or contradictions found.
